promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Forces in action (work, momentum, stopping distances)

questions.q: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second, so it is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²).

questions.q: Which equation correctly relates speed, distance and time?
questions.explain: Speed is defined as the distance travelled divided by the time taken.

questions.q: On a distance–time graph, what does the gradient (steepness) of the line represent?
questions.explain: The gradient of a distance–time graph equals the rate of change of distance, which is the speed.

questions.q: On a velocity–time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
questions.explain: The area under a velocity–time graph gives the distance travelled by the object.

questions.q: Which statement best describes velocity?
options: The distance travelled by an object
The speed of an object in a given direction
The rate of change of acceleration
The total force on an object
questions.explain: Velocity is a vector quantity: it is the speed of an object in a specified direction.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m in 5 s at a steady speed. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 m/s.

questions.q: Which of these is the approximate speed of sound in air?
questions.explain: Sound travels through air at roughly 330–340 m/s.

questions.q: A cyclist accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is the acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

questions.q: Newton's first law states that an object will stay at rest or move at constant velocity unless:
options: a resultant (unbalanced) force acts on it
it is moving in a straight line
questions.explain: Newton's first law says motion only changes when a non-zero resultant force acts on the object.

questions.q: Which equation expresses Newton's second law?
questions.explain: Newton's second law states that resultant force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).

questions.q: Newton's third law states that when object A exerts a force on object B, object B exerts a force on A that is:
options: equal in size and in the same direction
equal in size and in the opposite direction
larger and in the opposite direction
smaller and in the same direction
questions.explain: Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction force acting on the other object.

questions.q: A resultant force acts on a 2 kg trolley, giving it an acceleration of 3 m/s². What is the size of the force?
questions.explain: Using F = ma, force = 2 × 3 = 6 N.

questions.q: A falling skydiver reaches terminal velocity. What is true about the forces on the skydiver?
options: Weight is much greater than air resistance
questions.explain: At terminal velocity the upward air resistance balances the weight, so the resultant force is zero and velocity stays constant.

questions.q: Which equation and unit are correct for momentum?
options: momentum = mass × velocity, unit kg m/s
questions.explain: Momentum p = mv and is measured in kilogram metres per second (kg m/s).

questions.q: How is work done calculated, and in what unit is it measured?
options: work = mass × velocity, in kg m/s
questions.explain: Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force, measured in joules (J).

questions.q: The total stopping distance of a vehicle is made up of which two parts?
questions.explain: Stopping distance = thinking distance (during the driver's reaction time) + braking distance (while braking).

questions.q: Which of these would increase a driver's thinking distance at a given speed?
questions.explain: Thinking distance depends on the driver's reaction time, which is increased by tiredness, alcohol, drugs or distractions.

questions.q: A 1000 kg car moves at 20 m/s. What is its momentum?
questions.explain: Momentum = mass × velocity = 1000 × 20 = 20 000 kg m/s.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the weight of an object?
questions.explain: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength (W = mg), where g is about 9.8 N/kg on Earth.

questions.q: Two forces act on a box: 8 N to the right and 3 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
questions.explain: The forces act in opposite directions, so the resultant is 8 − 3 = 5 N in the direction of the larger force (right).
